title: The derived category of a monoidal Grothendieck abelian category is monoidal
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a Grothendieck abelian category with a closed braided monoidal
structure whose tensor product is additive, and assume that $\mathcal C$ has functorial
flat resolutions. Then the derived category $D(\mathcal C)$ carries a monoidal structure
whose tensor product $-\otimes^{\mathrm L}-$ is the left derived functor, in two
variables, of the tensor product of complexes on $K(\mathcal C)$ with respect to the
quasi-isomorphisms. It is computed by replacing either argument by a K-flat resolution.
The associativity and unit constraints are induced from those of complexes, and the
localization functor $K(\mathcal C)\to D(\mathcal C)$ is lax monoidal.

proof.text: By [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], $C$ has small colimits and exact filtered colimits. The ordered set $\mathbf Z$ is filtered, since $\max(a,b)$ bounds each pair, so its colimits are exact; countable coproducts also exist. Closedness means $X\otimes-$ has a right adjoint. The braiding identifies $-\otimes X$ with $X\otimes-$, so it too has a right adjoint. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] to each of these adjunctions: both tensor functors preserve the colimits required for total tensors and K-flat resolutions. All categories and colimits are taken in the fixed size convention for the derived localization.

source.place: First two sentences: closedness and the colimits required for K-flat resolutions; Stacks Tag 0038, categories.tex, lemma-adjoint-exact, is the colimit tool

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-total-tensor-homotopy] with the colimits just verified. Write $A=K(C)$, $I=\mathbf1[0]$, and $Q:A\to D(C)$ for the localization of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Its monoidal product is the direct-sum total tensor of complexes. Apply [lem-sfb-kflat-derivability] using the given functorial flat resolutions and the colimit preservation from step 1. Thus the full subcategory $P\subset A$ of two-sided K-flat objects is a left derivability structure, and for every $X\in A$ there is a quasi-isomorphism $p:P_X\to X$ with $P_X\in P$. This uses the homotopy-category part of the cited theorem; we do not assume a resolution functor descends to homotopy classes.

source.place: First three sentences: obtain the K-flat left derivability structure on K(C)

proof.text: By [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso], K-flat means tensoring on either side preserves every quasi-isomorphism. Hence $I$ is K-flat, since $I\otimes-$ and $-\otimes I$ are isomorphic to the identity by the unitors from [lem-sfb-total-tensor-homotopy]. If $P,P'$ are K-flat and $s$ is a quasi-isomorphism, then $(P\otimes P')\otimes s$ is conjugate by the associator to $P\otimes(P'\otimes s)$, hence is a quasi-isomorphism; on the other side $s\otimes(P\otimes P')$ is conjugate to $(s\otimes P)\otimes P'$. Thus $P\otimes P'$ is K-flat. Conjugating preserves quasi-isomorphisms because each cohomology functor preserves isomorphisms.

source.place: Sentences on stability under tensor and containment of the unit

proof.text: Consider $F(X,Y)=Q(X\otimes Y)$. When $P,P'$ are K-flat, changing either coordinate by a quasi-isomorphism gives a quasi-isomorphism after tensoring, by the defining preservation property in [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. Apply [lem-sfb-multivariable-derived-calculus] with $n=2$ and the two K-flat inclusions supplied by [lem-sfb-kflat-derivability]. It gives a bifunctor $B:D(C)\times D(C)\to D(C)$ and a natural counit $\mu_{X,Y}:B(QX,QY)\to Q(X\otimes Y)$ with the two-variable total left derived universal property, invertible whenever $X,Y$ are K-flat. Put $X\otimes^{\mathrm L}Y=B(X,Y)$. This constructs the tensor bifunctor before choosing its monoidal constraints.

source.place: Sentences on descent of the tensor bifunctor and its two-variable derived universal property

proof.text:
We check computation with only one K-flat argument. Let $f:P\to P'$ be a quasi-isomorphism between K-flat objects and $Y$ arbitrary. Choose $r:R\to Y$ with $R$ K-flat using [lem-sfb-kflat-derivability]. In the naturality square for tensor, the vertical maps $P\otimes r$ and $P'\otimes r$ and the top map $f\otimes R$ are quasi-isomorphisms by [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. Hence the bottom map $f\otimes Y$ is one too: apply each $H^k$ to the square and solve for that map using the inverses of the other three. For the other order, let $g:P\to P^{\prime}$ be a quasi-isomorphism of K-flat complexes and choose $s:S\to X$ with $S$ K-flat. In the square with top map $S\otimes g$, bottom map $X\otimes g$, and vertical maps $s\otimes P$ and $s\otimes P^{\prime}$, the top and both vertical maps are quasi-isomorphisms by the two-sided K-flat property. Applying $H^k$ and solving that square proves that $X\otimes g$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Thus $F$ restricted to $P\times A$, or to $A\times P$, inverts every coordinate quasi-isomorphism. The mixed cases of [lem-sfb-multivariable-derived-calculus], with one identity inclusion, supply derived functors $C_{P,A}$ and $C_{A,P}$ whose counits are invertible on the corresponding mixed pairs. Each mixed counit is therefore invertible on $P\times P$ as well. The criterion in [lem-sfb-multivariable-derived-calculus] then makes both $C_{P,A}$ and $B$ universal for the same two-variable functor with respect to the $P\times P$ derivability structure. The universal bijection gives a unique natural isomorphism between each mixed functor and $B$ whose composite with $\mu$ is the mixed counit on every pair of objects; hence $\mu_{P,Y}$ and $\mu_{X,P}$ are invertible whenever $P$ is K-flat. Given $p:P\to X$ as above, the isomorphism $Qp$ gives
$$ B(QX,QY)\cong B(QP,QY)\xrightarrow[\sim]{\mu_{P,Y}} Q(P\otimes Y),
$$
For a resolution $q:P_Y\to Y$, use $B(1,(Qq)^{-1})$ followed by $\mu_{X,P_Y}$ to obtain $B(QX,QY)\cong Q(X\otimes P_Y)$ instead. No flatness or boundedness condition on the other argument has been used.

source.place: Computation by replacing either argument; mixed-resolution argument underlying the K-flat comparison

proof.text: For each parenthesization $t$ of a tensor word on three or four variables, let $T_t$ be the corresponding iterated product of complexes and $B_t$ the same iteration of $B$. Compose the binary counits recursively to obtain $\mu_t:B_t(QX_1,\ldots,QX_n)\to Q(T_t(X_1,\ldots,X_n))$: at a root with subtrees $u,v$, first apply $B(\mu_u,\mu_v)$ and then $\mu_{T_u,T_v}$. At a tuple of K-flat objects every intermediate $T_u$ is K-flat by step 3, so this composite is invertible. The criterion of [lem-sfb-multivariable-derived-calculus] for $n=3,4$ proves that each $(B_t,\mu_t)$ is the derived functor of $QT_t$. The same criterion for $n=1$ shows that $B(QI,-)$ with $\mu_{I,-}$ derives $Q(I\otimes-)$, and $B(-,QI)$ derives $Q(-\otimes I)$; $\mu$ is invertible on K-flat tests and $I$ is K-flat. Finally $(\operatorname{id}_{D(C)},\operatorname{id}_Q)$ derives $Q$ since its counit is invertible everywhere. In each case the test functor inverts quasi-isomorphisms on K-flat tuples by the preservation definition [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso] and step 3.

source.place: Sentence on iterated derived tensor products in three and four variables, including the unit specializations

proof.text:
Derive the associator of $K(C)$ from [lem-sfb-total-tensor-homotopy] by [lem-sfb-multivariable-derived-calculus], between the two derived trifunctors of step 6. This gives an isomorphism $\alpha^D:B(B(-,-),-)\cong B(-,B(-,-))$ characterized, for every $X,Y,Z\in A$, by
$$ \mu_{X,Y\otimes Z}\circ B(1,\mu_{Y,Z})\circ\alpha^D_{QX,QY,QZ}=Q(\alpha_{X,Y,Z})\circ\mu_{X\otimes Y,Z}\circ B(\mu_{X,Y},1). $$
Derive the unitors likewise to obtain $\lambda^D:B(QI,-)\cong\operatorname{id}$ and $\rho^D:B(-,QI)\cong\operatorname{id}$, characterized by
$$\lambda^D_{QX}=Q(\lambda_X)\circ\mu_{I,X},\qquad\rho^D_{QX}=Q(\rho_X)\circ\mu_{X,I}.$$
For a tuple of K-flat representatives, identify each parenthesized $B_t$ with $QT_t$ by the invertible $\mu_t$. If an associator edge is applied at the root, its comparison identity is the displayed associator equation. If it is applied within a proper subtree, apply that subtree identity inside $B$; functoriality of $B$ and naturality of the root counit give the identity for the whole tree. Thus every pentagon edge $e^D_{t,t'}:B_t\to B_{t'}$ satisfies
$$\mu_{t'}\circ e^D_{t,t'}=Q(e_{t,t'})\circ\mu_t.$$
For a path of edges, substitute $e^D_{t,t'}=\mu_{t'}^{-1}Q(e_{t,t'})\mu_t$; each adjacent $\mu_t\mu_t^{-1}$ cancels. Each path composite is therefore $\mu_{\mathrm{end}}^{-1}Q(e_{\mathrm{path}})\mu_{\mathrm{start}}$. The two paths agree by the pentagon on $K(C)$. For the triangle, the unitor equations above and naturality of $\mu$ show that postcomposing its left path by $\mu_{X,Y}$ gives
$$Q((1_X\otimes\lambda_Y)\circ\alpha_{X,I,Y})\circ\mu_{X\otimes I,Y}\circ B(\mu_{X,I},1),$$
and postcomposing its right path gives
$$Q(\rho_X\otimes1_Y)\circ\mu_{X\otimes I,Y}\circ B(\mu_{X,I},1).$$
These agree by the original triangle; cancel the invertible $\mu_{X,Y}$. The cited calculus says natural transformations on $D(C)^n$ are determined on such tuples, so pentagon and triangle hold for all objects. Thus $(D(C),B,QI,\alpha^D,\lambda^D,\rho^D)$ is monoidal, with constraints induced from complexes.

source.place: Sentences on descending the constraints and their coherence identities

proof.text: Equip $Q$ with multiplication $\mu_{X,Y}:QX\otimes^{\mathrm L}QY\to Q(X\otimes Y)$ and unit $\varepsilon:\mathbf1_{D(C)}=QI\to QI$ equal to the identity. Naturality of the multiplication is the naturality of the derived counit from [lem-sfb-multivariable-derived-calculus]. The associativity axiom for this lax monoidal functor is exactly the displayed associator factorization equation in step 7. Its two unit axioms are exactly the displayed formulas for $\lambda^D$ and $\rho^D$, since $\varepsilon$ is the identity. Hence $Q:K(C)\to D(C)$ is lax monoidal with the same multiplication whose universal property and K-flat computation were proved in steps 4 and 5.

source.place: Last sentence: the resolution comparisons make the localization functor lax monoidal
